newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-NEW BIDS COMPLICATE FOREST'S FUTURE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NEW BIDS COMPLICATE FOREST'S FUTURE.

text.p: The future of Nottingham Forest was thrown into fresh doubt on Saturday when a further two bids were put forward for the struggling English premier league club.

Forest have already been the subject of two takeover bids this season, both of which were rejected by shareholders who had been expected to accept a third proposal from a consortium led by former Tottenham chairman Irving Scholar, author Phil Soar and Nigel Wray, the owner of London rugby union club Saracens.

But now the consortium has put forward an alternative offer which differs from the first in the balance between the amount of money it ploughs into the club and the amount it pays out to shareholders.
Either bid would require 75 percent shareholder approval.

"We've given the club and its shareholders a choice, both of which provide substantial benefits to secure the future of the club," Scholar said. "If the consortium's bid is accepted we plan to secure further funds for the club by a stock market flotation within six months."
Just as Scholar was outlining the consortium's second offer, an Indonesian-based businessman anounced he was launching a rival 22 million pound ($37 million) bid.

Nottingham-born Mario Cardinali, who was involved in a planned takeover bid from Indonesia last year, said he had 13 million pounds ($22 million) already and aimed to raise a further nine million pounds ($15 million) from Forest fans.
Under English law, the bids cannot be voted upon by shareholders for at least three weeks after they have been deemed legally valid.
That means the club, second-from bottom of the premier league before start of play on Saturday, faces more uncertainty before its future is resolved.
Fans have expressed their anger at the apparent reluctance of shareholders to accept a bid.
